### 1. Load Project Data 
```{r data}
#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <- read.csv("DATA/RAW/data_doctored.csv")

dim(raw)
str(raw)

data <- raw[,c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "Relationship_status", "preference_imp_health", "preference_imp_kind", "preference_imp_physat", "preference_imp_relig", "preference_imp_financ", "preference_imp_age", "cot_educ", "Gender_Equality_1", "Gender_Equality_2", "Gender_Equality_3", "Love_11", "Love_12", "Love_13", "Love_14", "Love_15", "Attract_importance_1")]


dim(data)
dim(raw)
str(data)

library(labelled)
library(codebook) 

```

#Prediction 1
H1: Categorical IV - Continuous DV

Individuals with higher educational attainment will have more progressive (less traditional) gender role attitudes. 

Educational attainment – The highest level of formal education reported for the respondent (cot_educ) ; Gender equality attitudes – Attitudes about gender roles in household labor and decision-making. The three items express traditional, unequal roles (Gender_Equality_1–Gender_Equality_3)

#Prediction 2
H2: Continuous-composite IV - Continuous DV
Higher confidence in relationships will be correlated with lower reported importance of looking attractive.
Commitment in romantic love (Love_11–Love_15) ; Importance of looking attractive (Attract_importance_1)


### 2. Check Participant IDs
```{r participant_ids}

###count na
sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))

###count blank
sum(data$ResponseId=="",na.rm=TRUE)

###count duplicates
sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))

###inspect records with missing or blank ids
missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
print(data[missingID,])

###remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

summary(data$ResponseId)

```

### Check Educational Attainment Variable
```{r cot_educ - Educational Attainment}

table(data$cot_educ, useNA="ifany")

data$cot_educ <- factor(data$cot_educ,
                         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7),
                         labels = c("None","Primary","Secondary", "High school/technical college", "Bachelor", "Master", "PhD/MD/JD or equivalent"))

table(data$cot_educ,useNA="ifany")
```


### Check Gender Equality Variable 
```{r Gender equality attitudes - "Gender_Equality_1", "Gender_Equality_2", "Gender_Equality_3"}

#Define variable group
geneq <- c("Gender_Equality_1", "Gender_Equality_2", "Gender_Equality_3")

sapply(data[, geneq], class)

#Make columns numeric
data[, geneq] <- lapply(data[, geneq], as.numeric)

summary(data[,geneq])

# Create matching reverse-coded var columns
geneq_rev <- c("Gender_Equality_1_rev", "Gender_Equality_2_rev", "Gender_Equality_3_rev")

# Clean and reverse-code gender equity vars
  ##1–7: Definitely disagree to Definitely agree. Before reversal, higher = stronger endorsement of traditional gender roles; after reversal, higher = greater gender equality endorsement.
data[, geneq_rev] <- lapply(data[, geneq], function(x) {
  num_val <- as.numeric(x)
  cleaned_val <- ifelse(num_val >= 1 & num_val <= 7, num_val, NA)
  
  # Reverse-code formula for a 1-7 scale (8 - score)
  return(8 - cleaned_val)
})


# Calculate the total (using reverse-coded vars)
data$geneqtot <- rowSums(data[, geneq_rev], na.rm = FALSE)

summary(data$geneqtot)

#Count NAs
colSums(is.na(data[,geneq]))

table(data$geneqtot)

#Calculate avg across 
data$geneqavg <- data$geneqtot / 3

table(data$geneqavg)

h1Data <- data[data$geneqavg & !is.na(data$cot_educ),
               c("ResponseId", "cot_educ" , "geneqavg")]

View(h1Data)


```


### Check Commitment in Romantic Love Variables 
``` {r Commitment in romantic love (Love_11–Love_15)}

#Make relData for participants in a relationship 
## (1) Dating , (2) In a committed relationship, (3) Married
table(data$Relationship_status, useNA = "ifany")

relData <- data[data$Relationship_status %in% c(1,2,3),]

#Define items in variable to check responses are 1-5 
## 1=Not at all , 5=Extremely
likert5 <- c("Love_11", "Love_12", "Love_13", "Love_14", "Love_15")

#check summaries and missing responses
summary(relData[,likert5])
  ##Max is 5 for each - good 

colSums(is.na(relData[,likert5]))


#inspect response frequencies for each item
for (i in likert5) {
  print(i)
  print(table(relData[,i],useNA="ifany"))
}
  ##note right skew, ex. Love_11 1=1994 vs 5=30279

#replace any codes outside 1-7 with NA
for(i in likert5) {
  relData[,i] <- ifelse(relData[,i] %in% 1:5, relData[,i],NA)
}


data$commitment <- rowSums(data[, likert5], na.rm = FALSE)

table(data$commitment)

#Calculate avg across 
data$commitmentavg <- data$commitment / 5

table(data$commitmentavg)

```


###Check Importance of Looking Attractive Variable
``` {r Importance of looking attractive (Attract_importance_1)}
#How important is it for you to look attractive? 
## 1=not at all important , 9=extremely important

table(data$Attract_importance_1, useNA="ifany")

sapply(data[, "Attract_importance_1"], class)
           
data$attractimp <- ifelse(data$Attract_importance_1 >= 1 & 
                            data$Attract_importance_1 <= 9, 
                                 data$Attract_importance_1, 
                                 NA)

summary(data$attractimp)

table(data$attractimp)

h2Data <- data[data$commitmentavg & !is.na(data$cot_educ),
               c("ResponseId", "commitmentavg" , "attractimp")]

View(h2Data)
```

## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units

var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Educational Attainment: 1=None; 2=Primary; 3=Secondary; 4=High school/technical college; 5=Bachelor; 6=Master; 7=PhD/MD/JD or equivalent, Now stored as a factor",
  "Gender equality attitudes: Attitudes about gender roles in household labor and decision-making. The three items express traditional, unequal roles, each. 1=Definitely disagree; 7=Definitely agree. Codes 2–6 are intermediate response categories. Values were reverse coded so higher values = greater gender equality endorsement.d"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Relationship confidence, scored 1=Not at all to 5=Extremely",
  "Importance of Looking Attractive, scored 1=not at all important to 9=extremely important"
)

```

H1 includes participants with an ID, a valid education category, and complete gender eqaulity attitude data. Factor level numbers in the
generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(h1Data)

```

H2 includes participants with an ID, relationship status 1, 2, or 3, and
valid nonmissing commitment in romantic love and importance of looking attractive values.

```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(h2Data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"data/processed_data/CLAProject_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"data/processed_data/CLAProject_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/CLAProject_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/CLAProject_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
